proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus is the right (entitlement) of an owner to alienate, consume, or destroy property. It is a kind of LegalRight, which is already typed as a subclass of Role (BFO_0000023). As a role, it is externally grounded in the legal/social system that confers ownership: it inheres in a bearer (the owner / the ownership relation) and is realized in acts of alienation or disposal. It is a class (a kind of right) rather than an individual instance.

entities.label: ActOfAlienationOrDisposal
entities.rationale: Abusus (as a realizable entity) is realized in concrete acts of alienating, consuming, or destroying property. These are processes (occurrents) in which the bearer participates. A new class is needed to serve as the realization target for the Abusus role.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a specific kind of LegalRight within the Roman-law property framework; LegalRight is already a subclass of BFO_0000023 (Role).
A role (realizable entity) is realized in a process; the Abusus right is realized in acts of alienating or disposing of property (BFO_0000054: realized in).

open_questions: Should Abusus be further distinguished from Usus (right of use) and Fructus (right to fruits) as sibling subclasses of LegalRight, building out the Roman dominium triad?
Is the bearer of Abusus best modeled as a natural person (material entity), a legal person (role), or the ownership relation itself? This affects how RO_0000052 (inheres in) should be asserted.
Should ActOfAlienationOrDisposal be split into sub-processes (e.g., ActOfSale, ActOfDestruction, ActOfDonation) or kept as a single class?
Is the intended scope historical Roman law only, or should this class generalize to any legal system that recognizes a right of disposal (e.g., modern civil-law systems)?
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus (ius abutendi) is the third element of the classical Roman dominium triad alongside usus and fructus, conferring on an owner the power to alienate, transform, or destroy the thing owned. In BFO terms it is best typed as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is externally grounded — it exists because the legal/social system recognizes and confers it — it inheres in a bearer (an owner), and it is realized in concrete occurrent acts of disposal or alienation. Because LegalRight already exists in the working ontology as a subclass of BFO_0000023, Abusus is introduced as a subclass of LegalRight rather than a direct subclass of Role, keeping the hierarchy parsimonious. A companion class ActOfAlienationOrDisposal (Process, BFO_0000015) is minted as the canonical realization target, linked via BFO_0000054 (realized in). Both are introduced as classes (kinds) rather than individuals because they represent types of legal entitlement and action, not named particular instances.
